kaps_punt: Farao's; Sosiale struktuur in antieke Egipte

items.bewering: Die farao was die heerser van Egipte.
items.bron: Harvard Giza Project, 'Social Status in Ancient Egypt' (giza.fas.harvard.edu/lessons/social-status-in-ancient-egypt/): 'the king, who in theory held absolute power'; Britannica, 'Hatshepsut' (britannica.com/biography/Hatshepsut).

items.bewering: Meestal was dit 'n man, maar soms was 'n vrou die farao.
items.bron: Britannica, 'Hatshepsut': a female king of Egypt who ruled in her own right c. 1479-1458 BCE with the full titles and regalia of a pharaoh; Met Museum, 'Hatshepsut: From Queen to Pharaoh'. Other women rulers (Sobekneferu, Twosret, Cleopatra VII) are few against hundreds of male kings, so 'meestal ... soms' is the right proportion.

items.bewering: Die farao het die land bestuur en die weermag gelei.
items.bron: National Geographic, 'How a single battle-and one young pharaoh-turned Egypt into a superpower' (Thutmose III personally led campaigns); Loprieno, 'Army and state' (University of Basel, edoc.unibas.ch): as Commander-in-Chief the king led the forces to war, though often represented by the crown prince. Harvard Giza Project on the king's absolute power over government. 'Gelei' at the level of supreme command holds.

items.bewering: Hy het ook groot bouprojekte soos tempels en piramides laat bou.
items.bron: Britannica, 'Hatshepsut' (large building programme, Deir el-Bahri temple); Discover Magazine, 'Lost City' (Giza pyramids as the tombs of kings Khufu, Khafre, Menkaure, built by royal work gangs).

items.bewering: Die volk het geglo dat die farao tussen die gode en die mense staan. Daarom het hy 'n rol in die godsdiens gespeel.
items.blok: Tussen die gode en die mense
items.bron: Metropolitan Museum of Art, 'Egyptian Art in the Age of the Pyramids' (Met publication): the king had a semidivine status and acted as an intermediary between the gods and people; Harvard Giza Project: the king 'was in many time periods understood to be divine'.

items.bewering: 'tussen die gode en die mense staan' (ruimtelike beeld vir die farao se rol as tussenganger)
items.blok: Tussen die gode en die mense
items.bron: Mapping checked: the image of standing between maps onto the Egyptological term 'intermediary' (Met, 'Egyptian Art in the Age of the Pyramids'). The lesson frames it as what people believed, not as a fact about the pharaoh, and pairs it with the temple-offering scenes, so a learner reasoning on from it reaches 'he dealt with the gods on behalf of the people', which is correct. It does not imply he was a god or an ordinary person, and does not need to at this level.

items.bewering: Prente op die mure van tempels wys hoe die farao gawes aan die gode bring.
items.blok: Tussen die gode en die mense
items.bron: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Temple of Dendur (metmuseum.org/art/collection/search/100004628): outer and inner wall reliefs show the 'pharaoh' presenting offerings to the gods; National Gallery of Victoria label 'Pharaoh: born of the gods': the pharaoh is depicted in most Egyptian temples offering to the gods (figures of Maat).

items.bewering: Die land se mense was in sosiale groepe ingedeel, met die farao boaan.
items.bron: Harvard Giza Project, 'Social Status in Ancient Egypt': the king at the top with absolute power, then government and temple office-holders, down to peasant farmers and those in servitude. 'Boaan' holds without qualification.

items.bewering: Ons noem so 'n indeling 'n sosiale struktuur.
items.bron: Standard usage of 'social structure' for a society's ordered division into groups; Harvard Giza Project, 'Social Status in Ancient Egypt' uses the same framing for Egypt.

items.bewering: Onder die farao was die amptenare en die priesters. Amptenare het die land help bestuur. Priesters het vir die tempels en die godsdienstige rituele gesorg.
items.bron: Harvard Giza Project: 'The highest levels of social status often came with government and/or temple offices'; World History Encyclopedia, 'Social Structure in Ancient Egypt' (J. J. Mark, via search excerpt): the king, then vizier, court, priests and regional governors.

items.bewering: Laer af was die skrifgeleerdes, soldate, handelaars en vakmanne.
items.bron: Encyclopedia.com, 'Scribes' (citing Egyptologist Alessandro Roccati): scribes who kept administrative records 'would have had a lower social status' than the highest officials; Harvard Giza Project on artisans and specialised workers below office-holders. Note for a person, not a fault: this is the conventional simplified pyramid. Scribe status varied with rank and period, and senior officials themselves held scribal titles (Harvard calls scribes a skilled, upper-class profession). Placing the record-keeping scribe the lesson describes below officials and priests is defensible.

items.bewering: Skrifgeleerdes het dinge soos oeste en belasting opgeskryf.
items.bron: History Today, 'Scribe Like an Ancient Egyptian'; tomb scenes (Menna, 18th Dynasty) show scribes recording the harvest; Mereruka tomb at Saqqara shows tax declarations before scribes; Google Arts & Culture scribe-statue entry: written records were needed to collect taxes and distribute the grain harvest.

items.bewering: Die meeste mense was boere wat koring en gars langs die Nyl verbou het.
items.bron: Harvard Giza Project: 'a majority of the population lived as peasant farmers'; Britannica Kids, 'ancient Egypt': nearly all the people were engaged in agriculture; British Museum, 'Farming in the Nile Valley' (Google Arts & Culture): emmer wheat and barley were the most important crops; Britannica, 'agriculture: The Nile valley': six-rowed barley and emmer wheat the main crops. Emmer is a wheat, so 'koring' is correct.

items.bewering: Daar was ook slawe en mense wat gedwing is om op plase, in myne en op bouprojekte te werk.
items.bron: Science in Poland (PAP), 'Egyptologist: The life of slaves in Egypt was not as hard as we think' (Andrzej Cwiek): slaves were mainly prisoners of war, sent among others to quarry teams; TheTorah.com, 'What we know about slavery in Egypt' and Loprieno's categories: conscripts and corvee labour on state projects, convicts sent to mines and quarries; Harvard Giza Project: enforced labour for prisoners of war; RAWI/AERA 'Feeding the Pyramid Builders': teams of local workmen sent to national projects.

items.bewering: Mense in elke groep het die lewe anders beleef.
items.bron: Harvard Giza Project, 'Social Status in Ancient Egypt': access to wealth, land and status differed sharply between office-holders, artisans, peasant farmers and the unfree.

items.bewering: Baie mense dink slawe het die piramides gebou.
items.bron: Britannica video 'No, enslaved people didn't build the Pyramids of Giza' (britannica.com/video/226777) exists to correct this widespread belief; Christian Science Monitor, 'Egypt says Jewish slaves didn't build pyramids' (11 Jan 2010).

items.bewering: By Giza het argeoloë 'n werkersdorp met bakkerye ontdek.
items.bron: Ancient Egypt Research Associates (AERA), 'The Lost City of the Pyramids' (aeraweb.org/lost-city/): Mark Lehner's excavation at Heit el-Ghurab, south of the Sphinx, since 1988; streets lined with workshops, bakeries, kitchens, warehouses and houses; Discover Magazine, 'Lost City': many bakeries where loaves were baked in bell-shaped pots. Lehner now also sees the town as a Nile port, which does not undo its role as the builders' settlement.

items.bewering: Hulle het ook daar naby 'n begraafplaas vir die werkers gevind.
items.bron: Discover Magazine, 'Lost City': Zahi Hawass found about 600 graves of tomb builders and 82 larger tombs of overseers and artisans, and Lehner's dig lies downhill from that cemetery; CBS News / Christian Science Monitor (Jan 2010) on further workers' tombs beside the pyramids, dated to the 4th Dynasty.

items.bewering: Die bewyse by Giza wys dat die bouers nie slawe was nie.
items.bron: Britannica video, 'No, enslaved people didn't build the Pyramids of Giza': most archaeologists and historians today think paid labourers, not enslaved people, built them; Discover Magazine: Lehner and Hawass argue the workers were not slaves (medical care, rotating peasant labour, burial beside the king's pyramid). Note for a person: some Egyptologists (Wildung) caution that the work was hard and partly conscripted. The lesson does not call the builders volunteers, and the block before it already says people were forced to work on building projects, so the two blocks agree.

items.bewering: Hulle was georganiseerde werkers wat kos en blyplek gekry het.
items.bron: RAWI Publishing / AERA (Claire Malleson), 'Feeding the Pyramid Builders' (Google Arts & Culture): the settlement had barracks that could shelter and feed up to about 1,400 rotating labourers, with weekly supplies of barley, emmer, cattle, sheep/goats and fish; AERA, 'Who slept here?': the galleries interpreted as barracks for teams; Discover Magazine: work gangs named in graffiti ('Friends of Khufu').

items.bewering: Iemand moes vir duisende werkers kos en blyplek reël en hulle in spanne indeel.
items.bron: Hawass via CBS News / Herald (Jan 2010): about 10,000 labourers fed daily with cattle and sheep; Discover Magazine: more than 20,000 people built the monuments; Britannica question page: as few as 20,000 workers with support staff; Lehner on crews divided into gangs and phyles (UCL Archaeology International, via search excerpt) and gang names in graffiti. 'Duisende' is within every estimate.

items.bewering: Die werk moes ook stap vir stap beplan word. Dit wys hoe goed die Egiptenare groot groepe werkers kon organiseer.
items.bron: AERA, 'The Lost City of the Pyramids': a 'massive workforce' of labourers, craftsmen, managers and administrators organised toward a single goal, with silos, bakeries and administrators' offices; RAWI/AERA 'Feeding the Pyramid Builders' on the scale of provisioning. A reasonable inference at this level, and the evidence supports it.

items.bewering: farao: Die heerser van antieke Egipte, gewoonlik 'n man en soms 'n vrou.
items.bron: Britannica, 'Hatshepsut'; Harvard Giza Project. Agrees with the study text.

items.bewering: sosiale struktuur: Hoe 'n samelewing se mense in groepe ingedeel is, dikwels van hoog tot laag.
items.bron: Standard sociological sense of social structure as a society's organised pattern of groups and ranks; 'dikwels' correctly avoids saying every society is ranked. Harvard Giza Project frames Egypt this way.

items.bewering: amptenaar: Iemand wat vir die heerser of die regering werk en help om die land se sake te bestuur.
items.bron: Harvard Giza Project on government office-holders; general meaning of 'official'. Accurate both generally and for Egypt.

items.bewering: skrifgeleerde: Iemand wie se werk dit was om te lees, te skryf en rekords te hou.
items.bron: History Today, 'Scribe Like an Ancient Egyptian'; Zinn, 'Literacy, Pharaonic Egypt' (UWTSD repository): scribes were literate through their profession and kept administrative records.

items.bewering: vakman: 'n Bekwame werker wat dinge met die hand maak, soos potte, meubels en juwele.
items.bron: General meaning of craftsman/artisan; Harvard Giza Project on artisans as specialised workers; AERA on craft workshops at Giza. Pottery, furniture and jewellery were all Egyptian crafts.

items.bewering: ritueel: 'n Vaste reeks handelinge wat mense elke keer op dieselfde manier doen, dikwels vir 'n god.
items.bron: General meaning of ritual (a fixed, repeated sequence of actions, often religious); Met Temple of Dendur reliefs show the repeated daily offering ritual. 'Dikwels' correctly leaves room for non-religious rituals.

items.bewering: belasting: Geld of goedere wat mense aan die heerser of die regering moet betaal.
items.bron: General meaning of tax. For Egypt, taxes were paid in produce and labour, not coin (egypt-museum.com, 'Tax in Ancient Egypt'; Google Arts & Culture scribe-statue entry on records kept to collect taxes and distribute the grain harvest). 'Of goedere' covers that, so the entry is not false for this lesson. If a person wants it exact for Egypt, labour could be added, but that is optional.

items.bewering: argeoloog: Iemand wat dinge van lank gelede soek en ondersoek om uit te vind hoe mense geleef het.
items.bron: General meaning of archaeologist (studies the human past through the material things people left); the Giza work by Lehner and Hawass in this lesson is exactly that. Accurate.

opsomming: Every claim in the lesson checks out against museum, university and reference sources. There is nothing to fix. A person may want to note two points: the order of the social groups is the usual simplified model (scribes' status varied with rank), and 'not slaves' at Giza is the mainstream archaeological view, which the lesson already balances by saying that people were forced to work on building projects.
